# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 2 lesson: the naive guess ("same as last round") beat my predictions in 4 of 5 rows. The one hit was a tie. So round 3 starts from round 2's measured numbers and moves only one number, C priority accuracy, because F4 gives a stated reason for it.

Default I chose: the paste does not give round 2 priority or cost numbers for A and B, or cost for C. Those cells use the regraded round 2 values, copied unchanged from the r02 results into `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` before the run.

## 1. Specify

### Proposal decisions

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 shows the merged tool hid the outage status check. Splitting it out is the only change to C. |
| P2 | Adopt, changed | The 10 hard tickets go in a separate "hard" set. Adding them to the core set would make the round 2 baseline useless. |
| P3 | Adopt as a default | D cost rose ($0.003 to $0.004) and F6 is open. The user can overrule this (see D1 below). F6 stays open. |
| P4 | Adopt | B missed by 0.02 at n=3, and that gap is inside noise. Five trials make each cell less noisy. |

### Requirements, round 3 (appended to `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3.1 | Config C moves the outage status check into its own tool. All other merged tools stay merged. | P1, r02 F4 | Code check: every C transcript on an outage ticket shows a status check call. |
| R3.2 | Add 10 hard tickets (mixed billing and outage) as a "hard" set. The core set stays exactly as in r02. Core and hard are scored separately. | P2 | Core ticket IDs and count match r02. The results show core and hard rows. |
| R3.3 | Configs are A, B, C. D does not run. | P3, r02 F6 | The Workflow config list equals ["A","B","C"]. |
| R3.4 | Each cell gets 5 trials. Split cells get extra trials up to 8. | P4 | Every cell in the results has 5 or more trials. |
| R3.5 | `grade.py` reads `label.priority`. The selftest has a case where the draft reply priority differs from the label. | r02 F5 | The selftest passes on that case. |
| R3.6 | Each hard ticket has one category in the answer key: the issue that blocks the customer. | Default, logged in D2 | The answer key has exactly one category per hard ticket. |
| R3.7 | Priority and cost are scored on the core set only. | Default | The results show no priority or cost rows for the hard set. |
| R3.8 | Trials cannot read graders, answer keys, or predictions. | Way rule | The transcript scan voids any trial that opened those paths. |

### Open decisions (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Drop D, or keep D and add a retry cap to fix F6 | Drop D for r03 | User |
| D2 | How to label mixed billing and outage tickets | Label by the issue that blocks the customer | User |

## 2. Predict

The verdict rule is the same as in round 2. Round 2 had 1 hit out of 5, so the 3-round stop streak is at 0.

| Metric | Set | A | B | C | Why | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | core | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.80 | Same as last round. Nothing that affects category changed. | `grade.py` exact match on `label.category` |
| priority accuracy | core | r02 value | r02 value | 0.76 | C can call the status check again, so some outage tickets move from P3 to the correct priority. It stays below r01's 0.78 because the other merged tools remain. A and B did not change. | `grade.py` exact match on `label.priority` (F5 fix) |
| cost per ticket | core | r02 value | r02 value | r02 value | Same as last round. C makes one more tool call, but only on outage tickets, so I expect the cost change to be too small to show. | Token count from the trial schema, times the price table |
| category accuracy | hard | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.64 | No baseline exists. Mixed tickets have two plausible categories, so I expect about 3 in 10 to be wrong. C keeps the 0.06 gap it has on the core set. I have low confidence in these numbers. | `grade.py` exact match on `label.category` |

Same as last round (from `r03-draft.yaml`): A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80. D (0.74) is dropped.

## 3. Evaluate

### Gates before launch (halt if any gate fails)

1. Grader selftest. The oracle passes. Empty answers fail. Wrong answers fail. The F5 case passes. The oracle includes the 10 hard tickets.
2. Control regrade. Rerun the current `grade.py` on the r02 transcripts. It must reproduce the regraded r02 numbers: A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80 category, and C 0.71 priority.
3. Dry run on 3 cells with 1 trial each: C on a core outage ticket, A on a hard ticket, and B on a core ticket. Check that each trial matches the schema. Check that C calls the status check.

### Workflow arguments (`spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`)

- `ROUND = 3` is one constant. No round number is written by hand in prompt text.
- `configs: ["A","B","C"]`. Each config uses the same model as in r02.
- `sets: { core: <r02 ticket list>, hard: <10 new IDs> }`
- `trials: 5`, `max_trials_split: 8`
- `budget_cap_usd: 10`. A trial that would cross the cap is skipped, and the skip is logged.
- Steps: run the trials, run code checks, scan transcripts for peeks, add extra trials to split cells, run failure analysis (including an F4 recurrence check), and run a completeness critic.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

I assumed 40 core tickets because the paste does not give the count. The yaml will use the real count. The estimate is 3 configs × 50 tickets × 5 trials = 750 runs. At about $0.004 per run, that is about $3. Gates, extra trials, and analysis add about $2. The total is about $5, with a hard cap of $10.

## After approval, in order

1. Save the prompt verbatim ("ok, next one") to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Write the spec table and `disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r03 specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with the header `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It also gets the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs A, B, C, every number, a Why per number, and `same_as_last_round`. Leave `r03-draft.yaml` as it is. Commit `SPE r03 predict: C priority 0.71 to 0.76, all else same as r02`.
3. Build the harness and pass the gates. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. When the completion notice arrives, commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
5. Close out: update the prediction log with "Which Why broke", update `failures.md`, add a "Proposed for round 4" table, write `r04-draft.yaml`, and update the README. Commit `SPE r03 learn` and tag `spe-r03`.

All commits are local. Nothing is pushed.

## Halt and report if

- The control regrade does not reproduce the r02 numbers.
- The budget cap is reached.
- A trial reads an answer key, grader, or prediction.
- The hard-ticket labels need D2 settled before the run.
